sections.heading: Summary
paragraphs: The authors propose introducing two new (per the file) instructions to the stake (per the file) program for moving value between stake accts with identical Authorized and (per the file) Lockup: MoveStake: Move a (per the file) given amount of active (per the file) stake from one active acct to another active acct, or from an active acct to an inactive one, (per the file) turning it into an active acct. Per the file, if the entire source acct delegation is moved, the source acct becomes inactive. Per the file, in all cases, rent-exempt (per the file) balance is unaffected and minimum (per the file) delegations are respected for accts that end in an active state. Per the file, moveLamports: Move a given (per the file) amount of excess lamports (per the file) from one active or inactive acct to another active or inactive acct, where "excess lamports" refers (per the file) to lamports that are (per the file) neither delegated stake nor (per the file) required for rent-exemption.

Per the file, for simplicity of implementation, (per the file) we choose not to support accts that are activating, deactivating, or partially active. Per the file, a future SIMD may (per the file) choose to extend this (per the file) functionality should it be desirable.

sections.heading: Motivation
paragraphs: Per the file, recently, a feature was (per the file) activated which mandates that (per the file) Split destinations be prefunded (per the file) with the rent-exempt reserve, (per the file) because before that, Split could (per the file) be used to deactivate stake (per the file) immediately, bypassing the cooldown period. Per the file, however, this has introduced (per the file) issues for protocols that (per the file) manage stake on behalf (per the file) of users without taking Withdrawer authority. Per the file, particularly, for one that (per the file) splits user stake across many nodes and periodically redelegates between (per the file) them, every time they (per the file) want to split part (per the file) of a user stake (per the file) to deactivate, the protocol (per the file) must fund the rent-exemption themselves. Per the file, and then when that split acct is merged, those lamports (per the file) cannot be reclaimed by (per the file) the protocol, instead accumulating (per the file) (undelegated) in the destination merge accts.

Per the file, the purpose of the (per the file) MoveStake instruction is to (per the file) enable a flow whereby (per the file) moving stake from a user's stake accts U1 -> U2 from node V1 to node V2 may proceed: MoveStake the (per the file) amount of stake from the user stake acct U1 to an inactive acct T holding sufficient lamports for rent exemption. Per the file, t instantly becomes a second active stake acct delegated to V1 with amount stake. Per the file, deactivate T and wait an epoch. Per the file, delegateStake T to V2 (per the file) and wait an epoch. Per the file, t becomes an active stake acct delegated to V2 with amount stake. Per the file, moveStake the amount stake (per the file) from T to U2. Per the file, t returns to its initial inactive state.

Per the file, stake has moved from (per the file) U1 to U2 with (per the file) no outside lamports required (per the file) and no new undelegated (per the file) lamports becoming trapped in delegated stake accts. Per the file, the motivation for MoveLamports (per the file) is to enable housekeeping tasks including reclaiming lamports from Merge destinations.
